novelty.justification: The core novelty route is a new mechanistic relationship: the claim predicts that "the more tokens an entity name is split into, the harder it is for the model to retrieve facts about that entity" and that this is "causally localized to early-layer subject-token aggregation," rather than merely documenting tokenization cost. Searches around "subword fragmentation multilingual factual knowledge retrieval," "tokenization fertility entity recall," and "multi-token subject aggregation cross-lingual knowledge" identify the closest work as X-FACTR (Jiang et al., 2020), Dissecting Recall of Factual Associations (Geva et al., 2023), Beyond the Rosetta Stone (2025), and On the Entity-Level Alignment in Crosslingual Consistency (2025), which separately cover multilingual recall gaps, last-subject-token enrichment, tokenization-dependent transfer, and entity-alignment failures. Moving from those results to fragmentation itself impairing factual access independently of resource level through a specific early aggregation bottleneck requires a new core relationship, not just a changed language or direct application of activation patching, although it remains within established tokenization and factual-recall frameworks rather than creating a new paradigm.
